items.text: rules/ast-grep/no-underscore-binding.yml holds one rule, id no-underscore-binding, at severity error with vendor/** ignored, whose message and note say it refuses because a leading underscore silences the unused warning instead of fixing its cause.

On an uncommitted scratch file with one underscore-prefixed binding in each of the 19 binding positions, the scan reports exactly 19 no-underscore-binding hits, and none on a bare `_`, a struct field declaration, a field initialiser or a field access.
`ast-grep scan --config sgconfig.yml` reports zero hits at the repository root of the landed tree.

sections.name: Bindings cleared by what they do

items.text: Every guard binding (a TempDir holder or an EnvCleanup guard) has a name without a leading underscore and is ended by drop(name) at the end of its test.

Every discarded error in a closure or match arm is left unbound, map_err is rewritten as .ok().ok_or(…) or .ok().ok_or_else(…) under the rule R4 states, and each site returns the same error as before.
Every value with no use is not bound: a bare `_` inside its pattern, an expression statement for a whole let, and no `let _ =` statement introduced.
Every trait implementation that ignores a parameter takes it as a bare `_`, and no trait declaration changes.
The two cfg(not(unix)) stubs, fsync_dir and warn_if_loose_permissions, take their parameter as a bare `_`.
cargo test --workspace --all-features exits 0 at the commit the build starts from and at its final commit, with the same number of tests passed at both.
